headline: Recommended $100,000 for arts grants, $72,824.03 for two special elections, and a 60-month trash hauling contract with Boston Carting Services.
summary: A $545,649 transfer corrects a budget error that placed six Code Inspector positions in Infrastructure instead of Public Health. Payment of $12,844.97 in fiscal year 2026 Medicaid billing invoices was also recommended for approval. Minutes of the October 20, 2026 meeting were approved.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 20, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Recommended approval of $100,000 from the Encore Artist and Cultural Support Stabilization Fund for Local Cultural Council grants, 5-0.
Recommended approval of a $72,824.03 supplemental appropriation for the two special elections, 5-0.
Recommended approval of $12,844.97 to pay prior year Medicaid billing invoices, 5-0.
Recommended approval of a $545,649 transfer to Public Health salary accounts to correct an allocation error, 5-0.
Recommended approval of a 60-month contract with Boston Carting Services LLC for trash, recycling, and yard waste hauling, 5-0.
Recommended marking the Urban Area Security Initiative fiscal year 2024 plan and allocations communication as work completed.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Finance Committee Meeting Minutes

Wednesday, October 28, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Wheeler at 6:00 pm and adjourned at 7:22 pm on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Link, Strezo, Hardt, Scott, and Wheeler), 0 opposed, and 0 absent.

Also present:

Rachel Strutt - Cultural Director, Nicholas Salerno - Commissioner of Elections, Anoop Malik - Health and Human Services Finance Manager, Michael Mastrobuoni - Budget Director, Eric Weisman - Department of Public Works Commissioner and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

Roll Call

- Present: City Councilor At Large Jon Link, City Councilor At Large
- Kristen Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt,

Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott and City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Finance Committee Meeting of October 20, Minutes

2026.

(ID # 26-1578 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

Arts

2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to appropriate $100,000 from the Encore Artist and (ID # 26-1514 ) Cultural Support Stabilization Fund to support Local Cultural Council grants

to artists, organizations, and schools.

Rachel Strutt, Cultural Director, explained that they distribute funding from the Massachusetts Cultural Council through fellowship and project grants, with approximately two-thirds of the funding going toward project grants.

She noted that the division supports a wide range of artistic disciplines and began receiving funding from Encore in 2022. This year, they received 179

- applications, making the selection process highly competitive. Chair

Wheeler asked whether the $100,000 would be placed in an account for use over time or distributed all at once. Director Strutt explained that the application deadline was October 15 and that the board reviews applications

before notifying recipients in late December or early January. Grant recipients would need to use the funds during calendar year 2027.

Councilor Link asked how grant recipients are selected and notified.

Director Strutt explained that experts in the field review applications based on their merit and potential community impact. She noted that Somerville

has a more robust arts grant program than most municipalities and is one of only four communities in the state to offer fellowship grants supporting

individual artists. Previous awardees have included puppetry at Argenziano, the Gilman Square Music Festival and the Arts at the Armory Performance

- Opportunity Program. Councilor Hardt asked about the Encore Stabilization

Fund, and Director Strutt explained that it functions similarly to a community benefits agreement with Encore, through which the city receives

$600,000, with $100,000 dedicated to the arts. Councilor Scott expressed support for the program. In response to a question from Councilor Strezo, Director Strutt clarified that fellowship grant applicants must live in

Somerville, while project grant applicants may live elsewhere, provided the proposed community arts project takes place in Somerville.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

Elections

3. Mayor's Request Requesting a supplemental appropriation of $72,824.03 to various accounts

(ID # 26-1545 ) in the Election Department to fund the two special elections.

- Nicholas Salerno, Commissioner of Elections, noted that the preliminary

election in Wards 2 and 3 will take place on February 2, followed by the final election on March 24. Chair Wheeler noted that the associated costs

- would be funded through the tax levy rather than free cash, which
- Intergovernmental Affairs Director Amanda Nagim-Williams confirmed.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

Health and Human Services

4. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to pay prior year invoices totaling $12,844.97 using

(ID # 26-1531 ) available funds in the Health and Human Services-Administration Ordinary

Maintenance Account for Medicaid billing and collection services.

- Anoop Malik, Health and Human Services Finance Manager, explained that
- the invoice was for fiscal year 2026 Medicaid billing and collection services.

- The final invoice from Public Consulting Group (PCG), which the city

contracts with to manage Medicaid billing for nursing and other services, was received late and covered services provided in schools. Director Malik

reviewed the attachment City of Somerville CIV-10045534 2026-07-21 and

clarified that the Medicaid minimum represents an annual amount, while the direct service minimum is quarterly. He noted that the department could

request monthly invoices moving forward to avoid receiving a large bill at the end of the year.

Councilor Hardt asked for additional information about the specific services included in the billing, particularly those covered by the school budget.

- Director Malik agreed to follow up. In response to a question from

Councilor Strezo, Director Malik identified behavioral support, orientation and mobility, social work, and speech and language services as examples of services included in the billing. Councilor Strezo also asked how the city

ensures compliance with HIPAA requirements when handling this information, and Director Malik noted he will follow up with a response on

- this as well.

- Budget Director Michael Mastrobuoni explained that Medicaid billing

requires specialized expertise, which is why the city contracts with PCG rather than managing the work internally. Councilor Strezo asked for further clarification on the decision to outsource these services. Intergovernmental Affairs Director Amanda Nagim-Williams offered to provide additional

- information in a memo before the next City Council meeting.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

5. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of a transfer of $545,649 from the Infrastructure:

(ID # 26-1524 ) Inspectional Services Salaries account to various Health and Human

- Services: Public Health Personal Services accounts to correct an allocation
- error in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget.

- Michael Mastrobuoni, Budget Director, explained that as part of Mayor

Wilson’s reorganization, Inspectional Services was split into Infrastructure and Health and Human Services. Six Code Inspector positions were

unintentionally transferred to Infrastructure and budgeted there rather than under Public Health. He noted that Public Health would run a deficit if the allocations were not corrected and that the adjustment would ensure the city’s financial records accurately reflect the positions. Moving forward, the Budget Office is working closely with Human Resources to ensure positions

- are assigned to the correct divisions.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

Department of Public Works

6. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to enter into a 60-month contract with Boston Carting

(ID # 26-1539 ) Services LLC for hauling municipal solid waste, recycling, and yard waste.

Commissioner of the Department of Public Works, Eric Weisman reviewed

the attachment Finance - 2026-10-28 BCS Presentation (with 26-1539 ).

Councilor Scott expressed strong support for the proposal, particularly the stable pricing for the next two years before an increase takes effect.

- Councilor Link asked whether the contract addressed the possibility of a
- strike in Somerville, similar to the neighboring Republic Services strike.

- Commissioner Weisman clarified that the contract does not include

provisions for a strike but stated that the department would keep the Council informed if such a situation arose. He also expressed confidence that the city is in a good position to avoid disruptions.

Councilor Strezo asked about the start time for trash collection.

- Commissioner Weisman noted that collection begins at 7:00 a.m. and cannot

begin earlier or later. Councilor Strezo expressed concern about collection during school drop-off times and periods of heavy traffic. Commissioner

Weisman explained that, as shown in the attachment, restrictions are in place in areas around schools to avoid collection during school drop-off and pick-up times.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

Communications

7. Communication By Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1548 ) Sharing the Metro Boston Homeland Security Region's (MBHSR) Urban

Area Security Initiative (UASI) fiscal year 2024 plan and allocations.

Chair Wheeler reviewed the attachments UPDATED UASI FFY24 EOPSS

Plan_REDACTED and FFY 24 Final Allocations_REDACTED and noted

that he requested these documents from the City of Boston in regards to the Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI) program, which Somerville has

gotten grants from before. He was specifically looking for information about the compliance requirements and believes these will be helpful documents to reference moving forward.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED
